corrected_text: ML Drift's AppleInfo::GetGpuFamily (gpu_info.cc) maps A14 and the M1 series to Family::kApple7; A15, A16 and the M2 series to kApple8; A17 Pro, A18, A18 Pro, the M3 series and the M4 series (M4, M4 Pro, M4 Max) to kApple9; A19, A19 Pro, A20 Pro, the M5 series and M6 to kApple10; A7 to kApple1 and A8 to A13 to kApple2 through kApple6; a GPU not in its table (AppleGpu::kUnknown) falls through to kApple1, which on Metal our build then replaces with the highest Apple family the device supports (ours: e5e4c6eb).
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: gpu_info.cc:739-767 and 822-847 unchanged at b7b856a0 (mechanical re-cite). Not listed, but G1 (e5e4c6eb) changes what an unknown name ends with on Metal: environment.mm:33-55 DeviceAppleFamily walks supportsFamily(1000+N) from 10 down to 2, and CreateGpuInfoFromMetalDevice calls SetUnknownChipFamily (gpu_info.cc:982-986, no-op for a known type). Corrected to say so.

corrected_text: ML Drift's AppleInfo constructor matches the lowercased Metal device name against a fixed table of names ('apple a7' ... 'apple a20 pro', 'apple m1' ... 'apple m6') by substring, keeping the longest matching key; a name with no match leaves gpu_type = AppleGpu::kUnknown and GetGpuFamily returns Family::kApple1. In our build (ours: e5e4c6eb), CreateGpuInfoFromMetalDevice then gives an Apple GPU of unknown type the highest Apple family its MTLDevice supports (supportsFamily, Apple10 down to Apple2, else Apple1) and an estimated compute-unit count, 6 on iOS and 10 on macOS; a known name's family still comes only from the name.
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: gpu_info.cc:683-737 and 764-767 unchanged. Not listed, but G1 (e5e4c6eb, 2026-11-17) makes the old parenthetical (family only from the name, never from MTLGPUFamily) wrong for unknown names: environment.mm:33-41 DeviceAppleFamily (supportsFamily by raw value 1000+N, N = 10..2, else kApple1), 46-55 calls SetUnknownChipFamily with 6 (TARGET_OS_IPHONE) or 10 cores when gpu_type == kUnknown; gpu_info.cc:972-986: kUnknown returns the set count (else 4), SetUnknownChipFamily returns early for a known type.

corrected_text: ML Drift's GetRecommendedMaxTotalSpatialSize returns 16 on an Apple GPU at CalculationsPrecision kF16 and 8 at kF32F16 or kF32; quantized fully connected builders use it as the largest destination spatial size (token count) that still gets an fc1x1 FullyConnected kernel, except that on Apple GPUs our int8 builder keeps fc1x1 up to at least 64 rows when the weights differ per height (attention products that read the INT8 KV cache as weights) (ours: 13def71b).
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: fully_connected.cc:907-922 unchanged (4, x2 for kF16, x2 not Mali, cap 16: 16 at kF16, 8 otherwise on Apple). gpu_model_builder.cc:1548-1556 at b7b856a0: B5 (13def71b, 2026-11-17) sets max_rows = max(recommended, 64) on Apple when different_weights_for_height (weights.shape.h != 1). The int4 (1645-1647) and int2 builders still use the plain threshold. Corrected for the exception.

corrected_text: ML Drift's GpuModelBuilder::FullyConnectedInt8ExternalWeights emits an fc1x1_int8_weights FullyConnected node when the destination spatial size is <= GetRecommendedMaxTotalSpatialSize (on Apple GPUs at least 64 when the weights differ per height, ours: 13def71b) or weights are ring-buffered; otherwise, with per-channel quantization, a weight sum, SupportsConvolutionInt8 and no kDisallow8bitConvs hint, it uses FullyConnectedInt8QuantizedWithSrcQuantization; else FullyConnectedSrcFloatExternalWeightsWithConversion.
note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: gpu_model_builder.cc:1516-1612 at b7b856a0: total_spatial_size = b*w (*h unless weights differ per height); fc1x1 when <= max_rows or ringed_weights; else the src-quantization branch on !grouped_quantization, sum_i, SupportsConvolutionInt8, !kDisallow8bitConvs; else float conversion. B5 (13def71b) adds max_rows = max(threshold, 64) on Apple for per-height weights (1548-1555). Corrected for that.
